analysis.title: Minutes confirm Fed to resume hiking in December
key_insights: CA-CIB expects the Fed to hike 25bp in December 2026 and again in March 2027, then pause with the upper bound at 4.50%. Risks are tilted toward consecutive-meeting hikes and/or a higher terminal rate.

October FOMC minutes showed the October pause was expected to be temporary. Almost all participants judged further rate increases would likely be appropriate, but the minutes gave no clear hints on pace or timing.

Governor Waller renewed his call for a 50bp hike in December, but the minutes suggest only a 'couple' of participants shared the view. CA-CIB does not think the data will be hot enough for a majority to back 50bp.
October PCE is forecast at 0.3% MoM for both headline and core (core about 0.28% unrounded). YoY is forecast to rise to 3.8% headline from 3.6% and 3.2% core from 3.1% on base effects.
Core Q4 PCE could land below the 3.4% median in the Fed's September SEP, but the data would still be firmer than the Fed wants and keep a December 25bp hike on track.
October retail sales surprised to the upside across all main aggregates, with upward revisions to September. Headline rose 0.2% MoM, ex-auto & gas 0.5% and control group 0.6%.
October import prices rose 1.1% MoM for a second straight month, which is not ideal for the Fed, though CA-CIB does not see it as a game changer for consumer inflation.
Initial jobless claims were 203k vs 202k the prior week. Continuing claims jumped to 1,763k from 1,693k, almost entirely due to Michigan, and may be idiosyncratic.
Housing is mixed. October starts rose 9.9% to 1,309k but permits fell 7.4% to 1,295k, the lowest since May 2020, pointing to continued softness.
Market pricing: December 25bp hike fully priced with under 10% chance of 50bp. Total additional tightening priced fell to just under 80bp from over 90bp the prior week.
Treasury yields fell on haven flows amid AI jitters. 2Y fell to 4.79% from 4.84% and 10Y to 5.06% from 5.14%, while the S&P 500 fell 4.5% over the same period.

Macro outlook: 2026 growth tracked at 2.3%, with 2.1% in 2027 and 2.0% in 2028. Pillars are household balance sheets and the AI investment boom, and a correction in AI equities is the key downside risk.

Inflation outlook: headline CPI briefly dips below 2% on base effects in 2027 and stabilises around 2.3%, with core near 2.8% through Q1 2027 and 2.4-2.5% by end-2027. This opens modest easing with 25bp cuts in Q4 2027 and Q1 2028 to a 4.00% upper bound.
Washington: government funding expires 11 December. CA-CIB expects a stopgap bill from the lame-duck Republican Congress, but not a comprehensive full-year deal.

risk_factors: A further correction in AI-related equities would pose downside risk to concentrated growth.
Hotter inflation could push the Fed toward consecutive hikes or a higher terminal rate.
Continued housing softness, with permits at the lowest since May 2020.
A government shutdown if funding is not extended by 11 December.
Rising import prices after two straight 1.1% MoM gains.

vol_and_positioning: Rates market fully prices a December 25bp hike, with a 94.1% probability for the 400-425 range and 5.9% for 425-450 as of 19 November.
Total tightening priced fell to just under 80bp from over 90bp a week earlier.
geopolitical: The Iran war has kept energy costs and inflation elevated, though CA-CIB expects limited second-round effects.
Hopes for de-escalation in Iran after the midterm elections are cited as supporting consumer confidence.
A US government funding deadline on 11 December raises shutdown risk, with a stopgap bill expected.

tension_points.bull_case: A hawkish camp, including Waller, argues for a 50bp hike in December given sticky inflation. Others want consecutive 25bp hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Most participants prefer a gradual approach, and Williams says he does not think the situation calls for dramatic action. Only a 'couple' backed a jumbo hike per the minutes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A PCE print hot enough to win a committee majority for 50bp would invalidate the 25bp base case.

theme_stances.key_argument: The October pause did not change the direction of travel toward higher rates, and sticky inflation keeps a 25bp December hike on track.
theme_stances.evidence: further action to raise the target range for the Federal funds rate
